BiblicalUsage: Chesheq is delight, the longing a heart sets on something it wants, and it is used both of kings and of the fearful. Solomon finishes the house of the Lord and all his desire, the chronicler lists all that Solomon desired to build, and Isaiah turns the phrase over to terror, where the night of pleasure becomes fear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe delight is a test of the heart, because what I long for most is what I truly serve. I hold that Solomon's desires built much and cost much, and that is the warning in the word.
